result.summary: Clamps transaction entry timestamps loaded from mempool.dat to the current time if they are in the future. This prevents loaded transactions from bypassing expiration under -mempoolexpiry when a node's clock moves backward across a restart.
result.problem: When loading transactions from mempool.dat, entries recorded with timestamps ahead of the current system clock are accepted as-is. Those transactions will not expire within the duration configured by -mempoolexpiry, remaining in the mempool longer than expected or indefinitely.
evidence: Author provides a functional test in test/functional/mempool_persist.py demonstrating that without clamping, a transaction written with a future timestamp preserves that future time across a restart with a stepped-back clock (PR description and commit c07124e5b5).
result.changed_since_previous: Diff and commit hash are now available; the implementation adds a std::min clamp in LoadMempool and a dedicated functional test in mempool_persist.py.
result.card: Clamps future timestamps to the current time when loading mempool entries from mempool.dat. Transactions loaded with timestamps in the future currently evade time-based expiry under -mempoolexpiry until the clock catches up. The author demonstrates the issue with a functional test where a node restarts with its clock set earlier than the saved entry time. Open PR #36540 proposes removing time-based mempool expiry entirely, which would make this change moot.

risk.why: Incorrect timestamp clamping during mempool load could cause transactions to expire prematurely or alter transaction eviction order.
